# Varela — A Calculus for Self-Reference (1975)

## Chicago 18 forms

**Full note:** Francisco J. Varela, “A Calculus for Self-Reference,” *International Journal of General Systems* 2, no. 1 (1975): {page}, https://doi.org/10.1080/03081077508960828.

**Shortened note:** Varela, “Calculus for Self-Reference,” {page}.

**Bibliography:** Varela, Francisco J. “A Calculus for Self-Reference.” *International Journal of General Systems* 2, no. 1 (1975): 5–24. https://doi.org/10.1080/03081077508960828.

## Essay use

Primary formal extension of the calculus of indications toward self-reference and a third state arising through self-indication. It warrants the claim that reflexivity can generate disciplined formal dynamism rather than only contradiction or prohibition.

**Passages needed:** introduction of the third state, autonomous self-indication, and the paper's claims for systems, logic, and epistemology.

**Claim boundary:** keep this paper's formal calculus distinct from Varela's later enactive work. Any identification between its third state and QL requires a displayed formal comparison rather than assertion.

## Passages and excerpts

The [Kauffman/UIC scan](https://www.math.uic.edu/~kauffman/VarelaCSR.pdf) has 20 PDF pages corresponding to printed 5–24. The title names one author, Francisco J. Varela G.; some online metadata incorrectly splits that name. Printed 5–10 and 21–23 were read, with printed 7 visually checked. Intermediate proofs and the complete appendix have not been audited.

<a id="varela-1975-calculus-self-reference-q001"></a>
### q001 · printed 7–9 / PDF 3–5

An autonomous third state expands the arithmetic; dominance, order, constancy and number govern reduction. Unique simplification preserves distinct values.

**Locator:** printed 7–9 / PDF 3–5.

### q002 · printed 21–23 / PDF 17–19

Temporal and systemic interpretations follow; frequency characterization remains further work. His metamathematical remarks do not establish escape from incompleteness for effectively axiomatized arithmetic.
